title: Jansen linkage leg
author: 3DCraft Jigs
description: A walking leg after Theo Jansen's linkage and his link lengths (his "holy numbers"), scaled to the hip height you ask: the crank axle's height above the ground. Drag the crank angle and the leg walks; the path of the foot's sole is drawn in front of it, terracotta in the stance and blue in the swing. Laser-cut birch bars and walnut triangles on brass rod pins with DIN 125 washers, stacked in four layers so nothing collides over the whole turn, on a double frame plate; one leg, or a pair half a turn apart. To export: File > Export..., Sheet of set: Cut sheet, birch plywood and Sheet of set: Cut sheet, walnut plywood, DXF or SVG, every part at true size with its holes drawn smaller by the kerf (turn your laser software's kerf offset off; lay the bars with the face grain along them). For a STEP of the parts, switch Draw the foot path off and export the model: the named set Leg parts is every part. The outputs list the brass rod to cut and the washers.
